talk_track: Ben Cole here. I've built the platform, DevSecOps, and FinOps layer under fast-scaling products four times — most recently taking Lexipol through a first-attempt SOC 2 Type II in a CJIS-regulated environment while cutting AWS spend 22%. Reflow's DevOps & Security Engineer posting says it plainly: 'As adoption scales, our infrastructure needs to be more secure, observable, and cost-efficient.' Read closely, that one role is being asked to carry three jobs — multi-tenant enterprise isolation, security reviews and audits, and cloud cost — which is where ops layers usually break: a single engineer with nobody owning the layer above them. And because Reflow captures how enterprise work gets done, your buyers' security teams will gate every deal on the audit evidence that role is supposed to produce, months before any single hire can ramp. Which of those three does the business need owned first?
